2. A PRECISE POSITIVE COMPOSITION RULE FOR BULK AND BOUNDARY CLOCKS
Let Q0,Q1 be nominal generators with the SAME invariant pi on the SAME actual class and original allowed transition graph. Let a0,a1 count ALL labelled firings. Use Dirichlet forms E_j(f)=1/2 sum pi q_j(x,y)(f(y)-f(x))^2, including the symmetric part if a generator is nonreversible. Suppose an actually established certificate is
 sum pi a0(f-pi f)^2<=G0 E0(f).
If a1<=C a0 pointwise with a computable constant, then Q=Q0+Q1 satisfies
 sum pi(a0+a1)(f-pi f)^2<=(1+C)G0 E0(f)<=(1+C)G0 E_Q(f).
More generally, E_Q>=c E0 and a_Q<=C a0 imply G_Q<=C G0/c. Common rational rescaling multiplies activity and form together and does not change G. Coefficients/rate inverse and physical time/firings still have to be paid; a free clock acceleration is not supplied. These inequalities are exact even with zero-change firing channels, which contribute to activity but not the form.

This identifies a real compatibility condition when adding a new nominal circulation to fix a different region: preserving pi and enlarging the form do not suffice if the new labelled activity outruns the old weight. In particular, controlling one pair of cuts, or adding arbitrarily high catalyst degree, is insufficient without the activity bound. The earlier one-degree versus two-degree tradeoff is a concrete example. The rule does not assume that every all-R equal-support clock can be dominated by some already certified boundary clock.
